expected_findings.description: `walk` now keeps a shared `RefCell` borrow of the node alive across the `visitor.visit(node, depth)` call, because `current` is bound for the rest of the function so that the loop can iterate `current.children`. Any visitor that takes a mutable borrow of the node it is handed panics at runtime with `RefCell already borrowed`. `DepthMarker::visit` in src/visitors.rs does exactly that (`node.borrow_mut().depth = depth`), so the crate's own `mark_depths` entry point in src/lib.rs now panics on the very first node of any tree. The previous form released the borrow at the end of the `let` statement, before the visitor ran.

notes:
Challenging: the diff alone is not decidable. Nothing in src/walk.rs says what a `Visitor` does with the node it receives; holding a shared borrow across the callback is only a defect if some implementation takes a mutable borrow. The deciding evidence is `node.borrow_mut()` on line 28 of src/visitors.rs, which the diff does not touch, and the second half of the picture is `mark_depths` in src/lib.rs, also untouched, which is the public entry point that wires `DepthMarker` into `walk`. A reviewer that stops at the diff sees a plausible allocation removal; a reviewer that enumerates the trait's implementors sees the panic. The other implementor in the same file, `NameCollector`, uses `node.borrow()` and is unaffected, so the file does not give a one-glance answer either.

Why the shipped suite misses it: both halves are unit-tested, only the combination is not. src/walk.rs tests `walk` twice, both times with `NameCollector`, whose `visit` takes a second *shared* borrow — two shared `RefCell` borrows coexist happily, so those tests pass. src/visitors.rs tests `DepthMarker::visit` by calling it directly on a node with no outstanding borrow, which also passes. src/lib.rs tests `node_names` (the `NameCollector` path) and nothing else. No test anywhere calls `mark_depths`, or otherwise runs `walk` with a visitor that mutates, so the one combination that panics is exactly the one the suite skips.

also_accept covers StateManagement and Concurrency; a `RefCell` borrow conflict is the single-threaded analogue of holding a lock across a callback, and reviewers reasonably file it under either.

Verified by execution: a throwaway integration test called the public `mark_depths` on a three-node tree. Output, with the crate as shipped:

    running 1 test

    thread 'mark_depths_marks_every_node' (122888) panicked at src\visitors.rs:28:14:
    RefCell already borrowed
    note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
    test mark_depths_marks_every_node ... FAILED

    test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.00s

The panic fires on the root node, before any child is reached, so it is deterministic and independent of tree shape. The throwaway test was deleted afterwards; `cargo test` on the shipped crate reports `6 passed; 0 failed`.
